course_name_original: Diseño y Verificación de Sistemas Mecánicos
course_name_en: Design and Verification of Mechanical Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to delve into the analysis of a specific scientific-technological problem, analyze it, identify the problem and provide a proposed solution.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Design and Verification of Mechanical Systems, both in written and oral form, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to prepare and publicly defend a research paper on a specific problem of Design and Verification of Mechanical Systems.

Ability to understand the behavior of different mechanical systems, considering factors such as their design, the type of stress they are subjected to, their operation, or the type of environment in which they must perform their service.
Ability to improve the behavior of an element or system in order to obtain novel products or products with better performance.

Ability to use the most advanced engineering methodologies, techniques, skills, and tools (numerical calculus, statistical methods, etc.) in order to improve conventional designs and obtain optimal solutions.
Ability to handle different resources and technologies that allow obtaining updated scientific information on the research topic to be developed.

Adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
To project, calculate and design products, processes, installations and plants.
To carry out research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Ability to design and test machines.
Knowledge and abilities to carry out verification and control of installations, processes and products.
Knowledge and abilities to carry out certifications, audits, verifications, tests and reports.
Define the necessary requirements for the design of machines and mechanical systems.
Determine the variables and parameters necessary to verify in the design of machines and mechanical systems.
Inspect and verify the assembly and operation of machines and mechanical systems.
Perform different tests on mechanical systems and machines, in order to study their in-service behavior.
Design mechanical systems capable of adapting to existing needs.
Ability to quantify the safety of components in service.
Handle scientific equipment necessary to carry out the inspection and verification of mechanical systems both during the manufacturing phase, and during assembly and use.
Organize a specific task and carry it out.
Write a scientific paper in a summarized way.
Encourage an observant and analytical character in the student.
Create research curiosity in the student.
Provide the student with an organizational and participatory sense for carrying out tasks.
Formation of an open, critical and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Inspection and verification of the design

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory/field practices and individual or group development tasks

assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a global grade equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 points is required. In ordinary calls, the final theoretical-practical exam accounts for 70% of the final grade, and a minimum score of 5 out of 10 in this exam is necessary to pass the subject. The remaining 30% corresponds to laboratory/field practices and individual or group development tasks. In differentiated evaluation and extraordinary calls, the written exam constitutes 100% of the grade, with 80% on theory and classroom practices and 20% on laboratory practices. Presentation, coherence in writing, and spelling will be taken into account in the final grade.
